# 1 Kings Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done — including how he had killed all the prophets of Baal with the sword.

**2** Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: "May the gods strike me dead if by this time tomorrow I haven't done to you what you did to them."

**3** Elijah was terrified. He ran for his life, all the way to Beersheba in Judah, where he left his servant behind.

**4** Then he went a day's journey into the desert, sat down under a broom bush, and prayed to die. "I've had enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life. I'm no better than my ancestors."

**5** He lay down under the bush and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."

**6** He looked around, and there by his head was bread baked on hot coals and a jar of water. He ate, drank, and lay down again.

**7** The angel of the LORD came back a second time, touched him, and said, "Get up and eat — the journey ahead is too much for you."

**8** He got up, ate and drank, and traveled forty days and forty nights on the strength of that food to Horeb, the mountain of God.

**9** He went into a cave and spent the night there. Then the word of the LORD came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

**10** He answered, "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I am the only one left, and now they're trying to kill me too."

**11** The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD, for the LORD is about to pass by." A violent wind tore into the mountains, shattering rocks — but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind, an earthquake — but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

**12** After the earthquake, fire — but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire — a gentle whisper.

**13** When Elijah heard it, he pulled his cloak over his face and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. A voice said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

**14** He gave the same answer: "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I'm the only one left, and they're trying to kill me."

**15** The LORD told him, "Go back the way you came, through the desert to Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king of Aram.

**16** Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king of Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah as the prophet who will succeed you.

**17** Anyone who escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.

**18** But I still have seven thousand in Israel — every knee that has not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed his image."

**19** Elijah left there and found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing. He was driving the last of twelve teams of oxen. Elijah walked up to him and threw his cloak around him.

**20** Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, "Let me go kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I'll follow you." Elijah replied, "Go on back. I'm not stopping you."

**21** Elisha went back, took his team of oxen, slaughtered them, and used the wooden plow equipment as fuel to cook the meat. He gave the food to the people, and they ate. Then he left and followed Elijah as his attendant.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **19:3-4 — the collapse**: Twenty-four hours after the greatest prophetic victory in Israel's history, Elijah is suicidal under a bush. The Bible does not pretend that spiritual giants are immune to depression. This is one of the most psychologically honest passages in scripture.
2. **19:7 — "the journey ahead is too much for you"**: God doesn't lecture Elijah. He feeds him. Before the theology, before the mission, before the correction — bread and water. God meets the prophet at the level of his body before addressing his soul.
3. **19:12 — the gentle whisper**: After wind that shatters mountains, an earthquake, and fire — God shows up in a whisper. The point is devastating: the same God who sent fire on Carmel now speaks in near-silence. God is not obligated to be spectacular. Sometimes the most powerful thing in the room is the quietest.
4. **19:14 — the same answer**: Elijah gives God the identical answer both times he's asked. He hasn't heard the theophany. He hasn't changed. God's gentle approach doesn't automatically heal the prophet's despair — but God moves forward anyway.
5. **19:21 — Elisha burns his plow**: There is no going back. Elisha cooks his oxen with his own farming equipment and feeds the village. This is not a career change — it's an identity funeral. The farmer is dead; the prophet is born.

— PNEUMA
